pr_title: ttl: do not remove all table TTL settings on RESET (ttl_expire_after)
pr_body:
Fixes #109138

Previously running `RESET (ttl_expire_after)` would remove all table TTL
settings if `ttl_expiration_expression` was set.

This PR fixes the schema changer to only remove all TTL settings on
`RESET (ttl)`.

Release note (bug fix): `RESET (ttl_expire_after)` no longer incorrectly
removes `ttl_expiration_expression`.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/110252)

One question before looking into the code in detail is it seems like after the change, only `reset(ttl)` will remove the TTL configuration, but what if a table has only `ttl_expire_after` set (so `ttl_expiration_expression` is unset), shouldn't `reset(ttl_expire_after)` also remove the TTL configuration, as we currently do?

> One question before looking into the code in detail is it seems like after the change, only `reset(ttl)` will remove the TTL configuration, but what if a table has only `ttl_expire_after` set (so `ttl_expiration_expression` is unset), shouldn't `reset(ttl_expire_after)` also remove the TTL configuration, as we currently do?

It was never intended that `reset(ttl_expire_after)` would reset everything - that was just a bug. To remove all configuration you need to do `reset(ttl)`.

> Good work! I have two last questions:
> 
> 1. If both `ttl_expire_after` and `ttl_expirataion_expression` are set, and we reset `ttl_expire_after`, the new code path, as I understand it, will be
>    1). Enqueue a DropColumn mutation (so we drop "expire_at" column)
>    2). Don't enqueue a TTL mutation but instead directly modify the TTL field on the descriptor
>    Correct?
> 2. If we only have `ttl_expire_after` set, and we reset it, it seems to me the same two things above will happen, but maybe later in descriptor validation, we will reject it, right?

1-1) It drops `crdb_internal_expiration` not `expire_at`.
1-2) It will not directly modify the descriptor because the mutation will modify the descriptor.
2) You can't reset `ttl_expire_after` if `ttl_expiration_expression` is not set - this did not change and there is a subtest for it.

>  It drops crdb_internal_expiration not expire_at.

Oh, my previous thoughts were wrong. Thanks!

> It will not directly modify the descriptor because the mutation will modify the descriptor.

This is somewhat surprising. Are you sure? In this case, `before != nil && after != nil` so no TTL mutations will be enqueued and the descriptor is modified right away. Or did I miss something?

This question and two of my unresolved comments are the only things I have. Thanks for doing this!

> > It will not directly modify the descriptor because the mutation will modify the descriptor.
> 
> This is somewhat surprising. Are you sure? In this case, `before != nil && after != nil` so no TTL mutations will be enqueued and the descriptor is modified right away. Or did I miss something?

This code is confusing because it may also be modified in the `before != nil && after != nil` block, but after that it will either add a mutation or change the descriptor immediately. I did not change this behavior.

issue_context.title: ttl: `ttl_expire_after` and `ttl_expiration_expression` should not be allowed to be set at the same time
issue_context.body:
We support two ways to effect row-level ttl: `ttl_expire_after` and `ttl_expiration_expression`.

Today, we support both to be set at the same time on one table. Although there is nothing wrong per se (we can still define the expected behavior in this case) but it is confusing and bug prune. I think it's best that we disallow this case.

PS: a bug that currently exists as a result of allowing both to be set:
If we create a table with both parameter set, `RESET (ttl_expire_after)` will remove the whole TTL configuration but the expected behavior is to just remove `ttl_expire_after` because we'd still have `ttl_expiration_expression` to vest TTL on this table. I guess this bug existed bc previously, we only support `ttl_expire_after` and resetting it means remove/disable TTL on this table so it makes sense to remove TTL configuration altogether. Later, when we added support for `ttl_expiration_expression`, we forget to amend that behavior.


Jira issue: CRDB-30800

Epic CRDB-29110
comments: We should not allow both at the same time. If ttl_expire_after is set, and someone tries to set ttl_expiration_expression we should emit and error saying both cannot be set at the same time, please remove ttl_expire_after and vice versa.

@dikshant these can both be set together to allow migrating back and forth.

I will fix `RESET (ttl_expire_after)` so that it does not reset all TTL configuration.

review_comments: Consolidated these cases into a switch to make it clear only one case will happen.
Do not assume `modify.RowLevelTTL()` is nil even though it will be based on logic to use direction=ADD.
Only initialize if we are going to use it.
super nit: "enqueue TTL mutation ..." might be better since the direction might be add or drop.
